procedure.description: periprosthetic capsulectomy, breast, with implant removal

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 19371 (periprosthetic capsulectomy, breast, with implant removal) with date of service 2026-04-05. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish a grade III or IV contracture or a confirmed rupture.

criteria.text: Baker grade III or IV capsular contracture with pain or deformity, or implant rupture confirmed by imaging.
The indication for the original implant placement is documented.
Symptoms documented for at least 3 months.

chart.text: Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

54 year old woman here about her implants. Discussed capsulectomy with implant removal and the options for replacement versus leaving them out. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now, seasonal allergies, reflux on omeprazole as needed. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Quit smoking 15 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Implants were placed in 2021 as part of her reconstruction after a right mastectomy for cancer, left side for symmetry. The hardening on the right started about 14 months ago and has gotten steadily worse, now hurts to lie on that side.
Blood pressure check. 123 over 74 today, 125 over 77 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Vitamin D came back 23. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Back to go over the MRI and the plan. She wants the right one out and both capsules addressed. Vitals today 142 over 88, pulse 64.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 192, LDL 153, HDL 42, triglycerides 147. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

Here with a cough and congestion for 7 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.4, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Pre-op. Consent signed for bilateral capsulectomy with implant removal, right side en bloc if the capsule allows. Labs fine.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 19. No ocular pathology noted.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-1 (complication); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
